Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". Old implementation:
```ruby
def ensure_connected
  super
rescue OpenSSL::SSL::SSLError => e
  raise unless RETRYABLE_SSL_ERROR_PATTERNS.match?(e.message)

  FIRE_COUNT.increment
```

New implementation:
```ruby
def ensure_connected
  ssl_retries = 0
  begin
    super
  rescue OpenSSL::SSL::SSLError => e
    raise unless RETRYABLE_SSL_ERROR_PATTERNS.match?(e.message)
    raise if ssl_retries >= @options.fetch(:reconnect_attempts, 1)

    FIRE_COUNT.increment
    disconnect
    ssl_retries += 1
    retry
  end
end
```

1. Added explicit begin/end block around super
2. Added ssl_retries counter initialized to 0
3. Added check: `raise if ssl_retries >= @options.fetch(:reconnect_attempts, 1)` to bound retries
4. Changed from re-raising as Redis::ConnectionError to using the `retry` keyword
5. Increments ssl_retries counter before retry

A new migration was created to remove the static default from campaigns.updated_at. Looking back at the schema, I saw:
```
t.datetime "updated_at", default: "2026-04-24 18:00:59", null: false
```

This is a static timestamp baked into the database default, which is wrong. The original migration used `default: Time.now` which was evaluated at migration parse time, not at runtime, so it created a literal static timestamp in the database. 

ActiveRecord manages updated_at automatically on writes, so this default serves no purpose except to give a misleading value. The migration removes this bad default.

Type: bugfix - fixing incorrect static timestamp default
